div.note: After a blank line follows, in a contemporary hand, Ælfric's pastoral letter ‘To gehadedum mannum’ (ed. Thorpe, Ancient Laws 452).

Besides differences already mentioned, the Latin adds details on church dues, mainly from II Edgar 2.2; a prohibition against selling men abroad (cf. V Ethelred 2) with an anathema on those who do; clauses on robbery, including the statement that the reeve who commits it is to pay double compensation; and a clause that every man, poor or rich, is to be entitled to law (cf. III Edgar 1.1).
